## Purpose

This procedure describes the proper use, zeroing, taring, and routine
quality checks for the laboratory balances in the EA Program. Correct
weighing technique is fundamental to virtually every quantitative
laboratory procedure. For calibration and verification protocols, see
[SOP-L200 Analytical Balance Calibration](SOP-L200-analytical-balance-calibration.qmd).


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All Mettler Toledo balances in the EA Program
  laboratory, including the basic balances (MS1602TS/00) and the
  precision balance (XPE205 DeltaRange) [@mettler_ms1602ts;
  @mettler_xpe205]
- **Does not apply to:** Portable field balances or calibration
  procedures (see [SOP-L200](SOP-L200-analytical-balance-calibration.qmd))
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure training compliance     |
| Trained Personnel | Follow this SOP, report malfunctions        |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## Definitions

- **Capacity (maximum load):** The maximum mass that can be placed on
  the weighing pan without risking damage to the weighing cell;
  exceeding the rated capacity will damage the load cell and require
  expensive repair; the MS1602TS capacity is 1620 g and the XPE205
  capacity is 220 g / 81 g (DeltaRange) [@mettler_ms1602ts;
  @mettler_xpe205].
- **Draft shield:** The glass or acrylic enclosure surrounding the
  weighing pan on the XPE205 precision balance; reduces air current
  disturbances that cause reading instability; always keep closed
  except when placing or removing items.
- **Drift:** Gradual, directional change in the balance reading under
  constant load; caused by temperature changes, vibration, or
  electronic instability; the balance should be allowed to warm up for
  at least 30 minutes before critical weighing.
- **Linearity:** The degree to which balance readings are proportional
  to applied mass across the full weighing range; verified during
  calibration per [SOP-L200](SOP-L200-analytical-balance-calibration.qmd).
- **Net weight:** The mass of sample only, after the tare weight of
  the container has been subtracted; what is displayed after pressing
  the Tare key with the container on the pan.
- **Readability (resolution):** The smallest increment the balance
  can display; the MS1602TS reads to 0.01 g and the XPE205 reads to
  0.1 mg (0.0001 g) [@mettler_ms1602ts; @mettler_xpe205].
- **Repeatability:** The standard deviation of repeated measurements
  of the same weight under identical conditions; a key short-term
  precision indicator; affected by vibration, draft, and sample
  placement position.
- **Spirit level (bubble level):** A small bubble vial mounted on the
  balance base; the bubble must be centered in the target circle
  before weighing; off-level readings can introduce systematic errors.
- **Tare:** The function that zeroes the displayed mass when a
  container is on the pan, so subsequent readings show only the mass
  of material added [@mettler_basic2023].
- **Weighing cell:** The internal transducer (typically an
  electromagnetic force compensation cell) that converts the mechanical
  load on the pan to an electrical signal; the most sensitive and
  expensive component of the balance; protect it from impact,
  overloading, and corrosive chemicals.
- **Zeroing:** Setting the balance display to exactly zero with an
  empty pan and no load; performed at the start of each session and
  whenever the balance is moved; distinct from taring, which zeroes
  the balance with a container already on the pan.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Dropping heavy items onto the balance pan can damage
  the weighing cell. Handle objects carefully and never exceed the
  rated capacity.
- **Chemical:** Some materials weighed on the balance may be hazardous.
  Refer to the relevant SOP for the material being weighed. Never
  place chemicals directly on the weighing pan; always use a sample
  vessel.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (when handling chemical samples)
- [ ] Safety glasses (when weighing chemical reagents)

### Emergency Procedures

If a chemical spill occurs on or near the balance, clean the spill per
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
before resuming use.

## Procedure

### Startup and Warm-Up

Allow the balance to warm up for at least 30 minutes before making
critical weighings (< 0.001 g significance) [@mettler_xpe205]. This
allows the internal components to reach thermal equilibrium.

### Leveling the Balance {#sec-leveling}

1. Check the spirit level before each use session.
2. If the bubble is not centered, adjust the leveling feet at the base
   of the balance.
3. For the XPE205, use the built-in leveling aid: **Balance menu >
   Leveling aid** [@mettler_xpe205].

### Zeroing {#sec-zeroing}

1. Verify the balance is empty and the draft shield is closed.
2. Press **Zero** (or **On/Zero**). The display should read 0.000 g
   (for the MS1602TS) or 0.0000 g (for the XPE205).
3. If the display does not settle, check that the balance is level,
   no air currents are present, and the pan is clean and dry.

### Taring

1. Zero the balance (§[sec-zeroing]).
2. Open the draft shield.
3. Place the sample vessel on the center of the weighing pan.
4. Close the draft shield.
5. Press the **Tare** key. The display reads zero and the **Net**
   indicator appears.

### Performing a Weighing

1. Open the draft shield (if applicable).
2. Place the weighing object into the tared sample vessel.
3. Close the draft shield and wait for the stability indicator.
4. Record the displayed mass in the lab notebook.
5. If using the XPE205 electronic results feature, tap **Add result**
   to append the value to the results list.

### Completing and Saving Results (XPE205)

1. Tap **Complete** to open the task completion dialog.
2. Select an option to save or print the results list.
3. Follow the on-screen instructions.
4. Tap **Complete** to finalize; the results list is saved or printed
   and then cleared.

### Shutdown

1. Remove all samples and vessels from the weighing pan.
2. Clean the pan and draft shield interior with a lint-free wipe.
3. Close the draft shield.
4. To enter standby mode, hold the power/standby key. The display
   goes dark but the balance remains powered on and thermally stable.
5. To switch the balance off completely, disconnect from the power
   supply. Note that the balance will require a full warm-up before
   its next use.


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### Leveling the Balance

Exact horizontal positioning is essential for repeatable and accurate
results [@mettler_xpe205]:

1. Check the spirit level before each use session.
2. If the message "Balance is out of level" appears, tap
   **Level the balance** to open the leveling aid.
3. Adjust the leveling feet following the on-screen instructions until
   the bubble is centered.

### Internal Adjustment (XPE205)

1. Navigate to **Methods > Adjustments**.
2. Verify that the adjustment strategy is set to **Internal
   adjustment**.
3. Select the adjustment and tap **Start**.
4. Do not touch the balance during the adjustment.
5. When complete, review the adjustment results.
6. Tap **Print** if a record is needed, then tap **Finish adjustment**
   [@mettler_xpe205].

For external calibration verification using traceable reference
weights, see
[SOP-L200](SOP-L200-analytical-balance-calibration.qmd).


## Waste Disposal

No waste is generated by this procedure. Cleaning materials (Kimwipes)
can be disposed of in standard trash unless they contacted hazardous
chemicals, in which case follow
[SOP-L003](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).

## Training Record

Before using the laboratory balances independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Demonstrate proper leveling, zeroing, taring, and weighing technique
   under supervision
4. For the XPE205 precision balance, also demonstrate use of the draft
   shield and internal adjustment procedure
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
